note.note:
ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Persistent fever with alternating hot/cold sweats x 7 days after return from rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago.  
  • No obvious local ENT trigger or exposure identified.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Day 0 (~7 days ago): Onset of daily fever, generalized myalgias, drenching sweats (incl. night sweats), nausea, ↓ appetite, fatigue.  
  • Symptoms have persisted despite regular OTC paracetamol + ibuprofen (slight, temporary relief).

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: No sore throat, dysphagia, odynophagia, voice change, or throat-tightening sensation.  
  • Nasal/ocular: Seasonal hay-fever history only; currently none.  
  • Airway: No stridor, dyspnea, noisy breathing, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling.  
  • Otologic: No ear pain or hearing changes.  
  • Neck: No neck stiffness, swelling, or tenderness.  
  • Oral cavity: No drooling reported.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No previous similar febrile illness.  
  • Chronic mechanical back pain (in physiotherapy).  
  • Episodic screen-related headaches/migraines.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: Seasonal pollen (hay fever).  
  • Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented; OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen per package instructions.

- Social context:
  • 30-year-old female nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol; regular exercise.  
  • Recent adventurous travel with trekking/cycling through rural Vietnam, including river/farmland exposure.  
  • Currently at home and able to attend central London clinic today.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No concern voiced; normal speech over phone.
- Mental status: Alert, coherent.
- Vitals and physical examination: Not recorded (telephone consult).
- Accompaniment: Not specified.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Febrile illness of unclear origin; high suspicion for malaria or other tropical infection acquired in Vietnam. ENT pathology unlikely given absence of localizing ENT signs.
- Evidence summary: Persistent fever + night sweats, rural SE-Asia exposure, incomplete protection by prophylaxis, no local infection focus.
- DDx (aligned with transcript and DDx engine):
  1. Malaria – High likelihood: classic hot/cold sweats, myalgias, rural exposure; prophylaxis not fully protective.
  2. Acute systemic viral illness (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Moderate: constitutional symptoms without focus; persistence > 7 days less typical.
  3. Dengue/other arboviral infection – Low-moderate: compatible travel history; incubation slightly exceeded; no rash/arthralgia.  
  (No conflicting information noted between transcript and DDx.)

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Patient to attend central London clinic today for in-person assessment and blood work.  
  • Labs requested: malaria thick & thin smears, full blood count, inflammatory markers; consider dengue/viral serology as clinically indicated.
- Patient instructions:
  • Do not return to work until evaluated.  
  • Maintain adequate hydration; continue antipyretics as needed.  
  • Seek urgent care (999/A&E) if develops breathing difficulty, altered mental status, severe rigors, rash, jaundice, or any throat/airway swelling.
- Follow-up:
  • Clinic appointment arranged by admin team; patient to phone booking number provided in consultation note.  
  • Results review and further management (including possible referral to Infectious Diseases) after examination.  
  • No ENT-specific follow-up required at present; advise to report new ENT/airway symptoms immediately.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: Objective vitals (temperature, BP, HR, RR, SpO2), targeted ENT/airway examination, detailed medication doses, malaria prophylaxis name/dosing, vaccination dates, COVID-19 test status.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None observed.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor pauses/over-talk; no inaudible segments affecting clinical content.
